## Walkthrough

This PR adds a new package `@typeberry/comms-authorship-network` defining an authorship↔network protocol and a TicketsMessage codec, implements a TicketDistributionTask in the network worker to broadcast signed tickets, and wires channel-based ports (DirectPort/ThreadPort) across worker bootstrap code (block-authorship, jam-network, and node orchestration). It updates worker API port handling, test coverage for ticket distribution, and bootstrapping to exchange networking/authorship ports and send tickets between block-authorship and jam-network.

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~50 minutes

## Possibly related PRs

- FluffyLabs/typeberry#827 — Modifies workers and protocol wiring for authorship↔network communication and tickets; likely overlaps bootstrap and protocol changes.  
- FluffyLabs/typeberry#897 — Adds ticket-generation flow in block-authorship that feeds into the new ticket distribution pipeline.  
- FluffyLabs/typeberry#720 — Introduces worker-API port primitives and Channel abstractions used by this PR for DirectPort/ThreadPort handling.

`@mateuszsikora` Excellent work! I've verified all 7 reported issues and can confirm they have been properly addressed:

✅ **Issue 1: Documentation** - `comms-authorship-network` added to `packages/README.md` between block-authorship and importer

✅ **Issue 2: Mark-after-send** - Ticket is now marked as sent **after** successful transmission (line 112-113 in `ticket-distribution.ts`), enabling automatic retry on failure

✅ **Issue 3: Epoch-aware aux data** - Implemented `getOrResetAuxData()` method (lines 58-72) with epoch tracking structure `{ epoch: Epoch, seen: Set<number> }`, which handles reconnected peers correctly

✅ **Issue 4: Port key in main.ts** - Now uses `AUTHORSHIP_NETWORK_PORT` constant instead of hardcoded string

✅ **Issue 5: Missing dependency** - `@typeberry/comms-authorship-network` added to `packages/jam/node/package.json`

✅ **Issue 6: Version mismatch** - Updated to `0.5.7` to match other packages

✅ **Issue 7: Port key in bootstrap-main.ts** - Uses `AUTHORSHIP_NETWORK_PORT` constant (defined as `"authorship-network"` in protocol.ts)

All fixes look solid! The key improvements include consistent port naming through constants, epoch-aware peer tracking, and proper error handling with retry capability.

## Comment by @coderabbitai[bot]

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Epoch-change aux-data reset misses disconnected peers — causes ticket skips on reconnect.**

Line 106 only clears `TICKET_AUX` for currently connected peers. When `pendingTickets` is cleared and new tickets start accumulating from index 0, a peer that was disconnected during the epoch transition retains its old aux-data Set (e.g., `{0, 1, 2}`). After reconnection, `maintainDistribution` will skip new tickets at those same indices.

Two possible fixes:
1. Clear aux data lazily: store the `currentEpoch` in the aux data alongside the Set, and in `maintainDistribution`, reset the Set if the stored epoch doesn't match.
2. Use a unique ticket identifier (e.g., a monotonic counter that never resets) instead of the array index.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```

connected peers so disconnected peers keep stale index Sets; update the aux-data
shape and consumer logic instead: change uses of connections.withAuxData(...,
TICKET_AUX) to store an object {epoch: Epoch, seen: Set<number>} (update
addTicket where you reset aux to {epoch: epochIndex, seen: new Set()}), and then
modify maintainDistribution to read the aux object and lazily reset seen to an
empty Set and update epoch when aux.epoch !== this.currentEpoch before using it
(so disconnected peers’ aux is refreshed on reconnect); adjust any code that
assumed aux was a Set to use aux.seen accordingly and keep TICKET_AUX,
addTicket, and maintainDistribution as the primary touchpoints.
```
